html:
SMTO-API-0004 — Runtime validation failed

GUID: 21d6221f-bf50-4997-b14c-e8094ba8cecc
Slug: validation-error
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • SMTO rejected a value it needed to continue, such as a setting, an option, or something in your request. This is a general message; the technical details usually name the value.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and find the value it mentions, such as a setting name, a file name or an option. This message is general, and the details show which value SMTO couldn't accept.
  2. If it names a setting you changed recently, open Settings, find that setting, and change it to a value its description allows. A setting outside its allowed range or format stops tasks that rely on it.
  3. If it names something in your request, check the task for steps that already finished, then send the request again with that value corrected. Earlier steps may already have done their work, and correcting the value avoids the same rejection.

What success looks like

  • The task or setting is accepted without this message, and nothing that finished earlier was repeated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting which setting or request you were using. Don't keep resending the same value; it will be rejected again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A ValueError or validation-phrased failure with no more specific registered error identity reached the legacy classifier and was reported under the validation_error category.

What this means

  • Legacy error classification maps ValueError or recognized validation phrases to this compatibility category after more specific structured identity is unavailable. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • Legacy error classification maps ValueError or recognized validation phrases to this compatibility category after more specific structured identity is unavailable.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original stage and bounded field/constraint evidence instead of assuming the user's prompt caused it.

How to fix it

  • Read technical_detail and the stage in Technical details to find the rejecting component and value, then correct that input or setting against its owning validator. Because this is a fallback category, register a specific error_kind at the raising site if it recurs.
  • Inspect the validation field and constraint, correct the input and submit again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual rejected value is corrected under its owning contract without replaying earlier work.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
